title: How to Set Up Kahana in an Afternoon
excerpt: You already have YouTube, Discord, Drive, or a reading app. This is the shortest path to putting a Kahana hub or club beside them without ripping anything out.
defaultImageQuery: afternoon light on a wooden desk with books
seoTitle: How to Set Up Kahana | Optimize Your Stack
metaDescription: Set up Kahana in an afternoon: create a hub, add files, list it or keep it private, and keep YouTube, Discord, and the rest of your stack.
content:
Kahana is the library in your stack. Keep the tools you already love. This guide is the shortest path to a working hub, a club if you need one, and a listing when you are ready.

Decide the job first

Do not start by copying every file you own. Pick one job. Kahana use cases include book clubs, selling a digital pack, ebooks, workshops, playbooks, journals, and course-like hubs.

If you came to learn rather than publish, skip hub setup. Open Library, save what you want to reopen, and turn on streak reminders later. See Kahana for learners.

Create a hub and keep it private

A hub starts private. That is the point. Add the pack before anyone else sees it: PDFs, video, notes, links, templates. Invite an editor if you work with someone. Step-by-step lives in Get started for creators and Hubs.

Put Kahana next to tools you already use

Do not migrate your whole audience on day one. Pin a hub or club link where people already are.

  • Video lives on YouTube. The hub holds the PDF, notes, and club.
  • Chat lives on Discord or Slack. Kahana is the shelf.
  • Email stays on Substack or Kit. Link the issue to the hub.
  • Checkout can stay on Gumroad or Stan. Dual-list the same pack if you want Library discovery. See your stack.

List it when the cover is ready

When the title, cover, description, and category are honest, list the hub on Library. Paid access is optional. Kahana takes 5% when someone pays. Details: List a hub and Paid access.

Optimize after the first week

Watch views, saves, and purchasers. Low views usually means discovery. High views and few buyers usually means the offer. Creators use Analytics. Learners use the Learning tab, Cognition streak, and reminder emails.

Then read a guide that matches the job: resource libraries, selling a PDF, book clubs, or workshops.
